Subject: Next steps: semantic probe and embedding evaluation for Ava Solutions

Hi Marta —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a proposed set of next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the POC.

Call recap (high level):
- Dataset: ~2M short docs (product descriptions + support KB).
- Query profile: 100–150 QPS peak, mostly short queries (2–8 tokens).
- Latency target for retrieval (top-5): median <50ms; 95th <120ms.
- Quality target: baseline goal is recall@10 >= 0.80 on your relevance labels; strong preference for improvements in MRR and NDCG.

Initial embedding candidates (we’ll run a small probe across each):
- redwood-embed-small-v2 — 512 dims, low-cost, strong throughput.
- redwood-embed-iso-768 — 768 dims, better semantic separation for longer docs.
- open-simcse-mini-256 — 256 dims, compact index footprint (tradeoff: quality vs cost).

Evaluation plan (what we’ll measure):
- Data: 200 labelled probe queries provided by your SME + 1k synthetic queries for robustness testing.
- Metrics: recall@1/5/10, MRR, NDCG@10, median/95th retrieval latency, index size (GB), and cost per 1M queries.
- Indexing: test both cosine and dot-product similarity; initial index engine: FAISS HNSW.
- Dimensionality checks: run PCA to 256/384 for candidates to evaluate tradeoffs.
- Drift checks: baseline distribution + monthly KS test for cosine similarity distribution.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short sample_queries.csv (format: query, expected_doc_id, intent_tag) so we can align on labels.

Proposed next steps (ask):
1) Grant us read-only S3 access to a representative .parquet (50k docs) so we can run the probe (temporary creds ok).
2) Confirm the 2-week POC window (we suggest Jun 8–Jun 21).
3) Confirm any compliance requirements (SOC2 / IP constraints) so we can scope data handling.

If that all looks good I’ll loop in Marissa to finalize the eval script and Rishi on performance sizing / Dedicated pricing.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Karthik — putting a quick tech plan below so we can be operational as soon as we get the S3 sample. High level notes for the evaluation runbook: 

1) Environment & infra
- Use FAISS HNSW on a 1 shard index for the 50k probe; scale to 128 shard simulation for production sizing.
- Run CPU-based building for speed; run GPU-accelerated nearest-neighbor search for latency experiments (NVIDIA A10 / A40 baseline).

2) Scripts & reproducibility
- eval/run_probe.py (deterministic seed + config per model candidate).
- Output: per-query retrieval list, per-model metric summary, latency histograms.
- Attach: semantic_eval_plan.md (includes reproducible commands and expected outputs).

3) Metrics and thresholds
- Primary: recall@10 >= 0.80 (target), MRR delta vs baseline >= +0.05 to be considered significant.
- Secondary: NDCG@10, median retrieval latency, index storage (GB) per million docs.

4) Dimensionality & compression experiments
- Baseline dims: 256/512/768 tests.
- Run PCA to 256 and 384 to check quality drop vs index size savings.
- Try product quantization (PQ) for 512/768 runs to estimate throughput gains.

5) Drift and ongoing monitoring
- Snapshot baseline similarity distribution; monthly KS test and 7-day rolling median for cosine similarities.
- Add alert if KS p-value < 0.01 or median similarity shifts by > 0.05.

Attachments included for the POC: semantic_eval_plan.md, evaluation-metrics.md, small-run shell script (semantic_probe.sh). I’ve noted the FAISS configuration we should try first in the plan.

I’ll prep a one-page runbook for the customer-facing kickoff and include a checklist for SOC2 redlines.

-Marissa
